response.title: Harborlight FY2026 Results and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: Who we served
segments.text: Harborlight reached more adult learners in fiscal year 2026. Staff now ask the board to fund a sixth site. Here is where things stand. Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners at five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. Of those learners, 412 worked toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. All five sites sit in local neighborhoods.

segments.heading: Gains for learners
segments.text: Learners made real progress. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels. The CASAS assessment measures those gains. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. That is the most in the organization's history. Volunteers made much of this work possible. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight also employs 11 full-time staff, including four site coordinators.

segments.heading: Money and reserves
segments.text: Next, the money. Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 came to $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. The cost per learner was $1,237. The board should note one concern. The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months. That leaves reserves short of the target.

segments.heading: The waitlist
segments.text: Demand still outruns space. At year end, 287 adults sat on the waitlist. Most of them were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks. The staff plan takes aim at this gap. A learner at the Riverside site put the stakes in plain words. Quote. "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: What staff recommend
segments.text: Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. That budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21. Board members also asked for a short deck. They plan to use it with funders when they discuss the sixth site.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, with an average wait of nine weeks. Third, staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 for a sixth site. At the same time, reserves stand at 3.2 months against a target of 4 months.
